newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - DEC 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - DEC 24.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
KATHIMERINI

--Commercial banks forecast a new round of interest rate cuts for the New Year following yesterday's decision by the finance ministry to reduce rates on the final issue of state titles for 1996. The banks, however, will wait for the Bank of Greece to make the first move in the interbank market, where rates have been at high levels since September.
--The Hatzioannou brothers yesterday bought 66.67 percent of Iliofin from the National Bank, a deal brokered by National Securities and Kappa.

--The end of the farmers' blockades has freed the government to deal with issues such as the operation of the market, banking and insurance sectors one by one, beginning in the New Year. The two last hurdles are the passing by Parliament of new bills on taxation and public expenditures.

--Prime Minister Costas Simitis, meanwhile, met yesterday with representatives of farmers' groups, promising to personally follow developments in the farm sector and to work towards reform rather than pay-outs.
IMERISIA

--The final touches on the new taxation regime for state titles have been put: the government's new bill ensures that noboy will be able to avoid paying the 7.5 percent tax on treasury bills, even if that means foreign investors pay tax twice. However, talks with the European Union are still under way on the taxation of bonds.

--The sale of the Bank of Attica saga finally came to an end yesterday when the majority of shares were sold for 9.4 billion drachmas: the Commercial Bank maintains a 20 percent stake and management for the next five years.

--At least five brokerage firms are facing problems, according to the bourse supervisory authority. The report, Deputy National Economy Minister Apostolos Fotiadis says, will be released on January 15.
KERDOS
--A finance ministry circular on the taxation of state titles as of January 1 was issued yesterday, defining procedures.
--Moody's upgrading of Greece's sovereign ceiling on foreign loans has brought Greece closer to its target of being included in the second wave of countries to adopt a common European currency.

--The government is optimistic about the course of inflation in the first half of 1997 - now assured that the farmers' protests will have no repercussions on prices - and that the national economy ministry's forecast of 6.0 percent inflation at the end of the first quarter will be met.
EXPRESS

--The government's insistence on not giving in to the farmers' will have long-term advantages, international market representatives say. Simitis tells farmers yesterday that the era of hand-outs from the state is over, as he begins dialogue.
NAFTEMBORIKI

--Ailing state-run firms unable to pay wages and Christmas bonuses were the focus of activity yesterday at the development ministry. The firms are on line for privatisation but the time-consuming process means that they are still sucking up funds.
--Absroption rates for the Community Support Framework funds were higher this year and will be the highest ever in 1997, sources say.
--Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
